t: Three runways: a long east–west one, a northeast–southwest one, and a shorter diagonal that crosses the northeast–southwest one, so they fan out like a rough star.
Sits on a high, brown desert mesa, with the Sandia Mountains rising straight up on the east side.
Kirtland Air Force Base shares the field, so military ramps and hangars sit right beside the airline terminal.
The green ribbon of the Rio Grande valley is a few miles to the west.
KABQ.w: Albuquerque is famous for its October hot-air balloon fiesta.

t: Two runways cross in an X, a long north–south one and a shorter east–west one.
Surrounded by woods and suburbs northwest of Albany, with no big body of water next to it.
The Hudson River and the city are to the southeast, about eight miles away.
KALB.w: Albany is in New York, and bagels are a New York classic.

t: Five long runways, all parallel and running east–west, the airport's strongest clue.
The terminal is a long row of parallel concourses (T, A, B, C, D, E, F) stretching out like fingers between the two middle runways.
Sits just south of downtown Atlanta, hemmed in by dense highways, rental-car lots and industrial blocks.
KATL.w: Atlantans are the people of Atlanta; the lemonade nods to sweet Georgia drinks.

t: Two long parallel runways running north–south, the main one over 12,000 ft.
State Highway 71 runs along the airport's north side, and the Colorado River passes just north of it.
This is the former Bergstrom Air Force Base, so the land is flat and open with wide aprons southeast of downtown Austin.
KAUS.w: “Keep Austin Weird” is the city's famous slogan.

t: Two runways cross in an X, with the longer one running northeast–southwest.
Sits in Windsor Locks north of Hartford, close to the Connecticut River, which runs just east of the field.
Surrounded by flat, wooded New England land and highways, not by mountains or open water.
KBDL.w: No local link: the silly kettle picture is just a hook for B-D-L. (Bradley is in Windsor Locks, Connecticut.)

t: Two runways: a long one running northeast–southwest and a shorter north–south one that crosses it.
Sits northeast of downtown Birmingham among wooded, rolling Appalachian foothills.
KBHM.w: No local link: hot muffins are a tasty picture for B-H-M.

t: Four runways: three long parallel ones running north–south, plus a longer diagonal runway cutting across them from the northwest to the southeast.
Interstate 40 runs along the airport's north side.
Sits southeast of downtown Nashville, with wooded suburbs on all sides.
KBNA.w: Nashville is Music City, home of country music and banjos.

t: Two long parallel runways running east-southeast to west-northwest, close together and almost the same length.
A dry, tan landscape with the Boise foothills to the north; the Boise River passes north of the field.
Gowen Field's Air National Guard ramp, with military aircraft and hangars, sits along the south side.
KBOI.w: Boise is known for its outdoors: the river, foothills and ski slopes.

t: Built on a peninsula of landfill poking into Boston Harbor, with water on several sides and the downtown skyline right across the water to the west.
Five runways in a pinwheel, with pairs crossing each other and several pointing straight out into the harbor.
The terminals curve in a horseshoe around a central parking area.
KBOS.w: Boston is famous for seafood like clam chowder and lobster.

t: Two runways cross in an X, the longer one running northeast–southwest.
Sits east of downtown Buffalo among dense suburbs such as Cheektowaga, with Lake Erie about ten miles to the west.
KBUF.w: Buffalo is the home of Buffalo wings.

t: Two runways cross at nearly a right angle, and both are short for a jet airport, under 7,000 ft.
Hemmed in by dense Los Angeles suburbs on every side, with the Verdugo Mountains rising to the northeast.
Interstate 5 runs along the airport's east side.
KBUR.w: Burbank is a movie-studio town, so cameras and reality TV fit.

t: Three runways: a long east–west one crossed by a long northwest–southeast one, with a shorter parallel one beside it.
Sits southwest of Baltimore, between Baltimore and Washington, in a sprawl of highways, warehouses and suburbs.
KBWI.w: BWI is Baltimore/Washington International; the ice cream just gives you the W and I.

t: Two runways cross in an X, one running northwest–southeast and one northeast–southwest.
Joint Base Charleston shares the field, so large gray military transports (C-17s) sit on a ramp on the east side.
Flat Lowcountry land with marshes and creeks around it, and Interstate 526 passing just south.
KCHS.w: Charleston is known for southern cooking, like hushpuppies.

t: Two long parallel runways running northeast–southwest, plus a shorter east–west runway.
NASA Glenn Research Center sits right next to the airport.
On the west side of Cleveland, with suburbs all around; Lake Erie is about ten miles north.
KCLE.w: Cleveland is home to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, so think loud electric guitars.

t: Three parallel north–south runways, with the shortest one set farther to the west.
Interstate 85 runs just north of the airport, and the Catawba River (Lake Wylie) is a short way west.
A large hub terminal with long concourses reaching out into the field.
KCLT.w: Charlotte is NASCAR country: cars racing laps around tracks.

t: Two parallel runways running east–west, one noticeably longer than the other.
Interstate 270, the outer belt loop, runs along the airport's east side.
Surrounded by flat Ohio farmland and suburbs east of downtown Columbus.
KCMH.w: No local link: “call Mom home” is just easy to say and picture for C-M-H. (Columbus is in Ohio.)

t: Three runways: two long parallel ones running north–south and a diagonal one running northwest–southeast.
Pikes Peak and the Rocky Mountains rise right to the west, with open plains to the east.
Peterson Space Force Base shares the field on the west side, with military hangars and aircraft.
KCOS.w: Colorado Springs sits under Pikes Peak, so climbing over summits fits.

t: Four runways: three parallel north–south runways and a long east–west runway that crosses them.
Sits in Kentucky, about ten miles southwest of downtown Cincinnati, with the Ohio River to the north.
DHL's huge hub ramp, full of cargo planes and sorting buildings, is on the field itself.
KCVG.w: Cincinnati is famous for its chili.

t: Two parallel runways running northwest–southeast, with the terminal along the east side.
A small airport tucked into the city, just northwest of downtown Dallas, ringed by streets, warehouses and neighborhoods.
Bachman Lake sits right next to the northwest corner of the field.
KDAL.w: Dallas is cowboy country, and Texas distances mean driving a lot.

t: Right on the Potomac River, with the river along the airport's east side and Washington, DC across the water.
Three short runways in a rough triangle: one runs north–south and two others cross it at angles.
The Pentagon is about a mile and a half to the north, and Arlington's high-rises are just beyond the airport's northwest side.
KDCA.w: Washington, DC is where Congress meets, and adjourns.

t: Six long runways spread over an enormous flat site: four run north–south and two run east–west.
The terminal is a long central building under a white, peaked, tent-like roof, with three parallel concourses (A, B, C) lined up beside it.
Far out on open plains northeast of Denver, with nothing but fields around it and the Rocky Mountains on the western horizon.
KDEN.w: Denver is the Mile High City, so it is elevated.

t: Seven runways: five long parallel ones running north–south and two running northwest–southeast.
The terminals are semicircular horseshoes built along a long central spine road, one after another.
Enormous: the airport covers more land than the island of Manhattan, set between Dallas and Fort Worth.
KDFW.w: The words are the airport itself: Dallas and Fort Worth.

t: Two runways cross in an X, running northeast–southwest and northwest–southeast.
Sits southwest of downtown Des Moines in flat Iowa farmland and neighborhoods, with no big lake or mountains nearby.
KDSM.w: Des Moines is in Iowa corn country, so dancing kernels fit.

t: Six runways: four long parallel ones running north-northeast to south-southwest, crossed by two east–west runways.
The main terminal is an extremely long, narrow ribbon of gates about a mile long, with a train in the middle.
Interstate 94 runs along the airport's north side, and the surroundings are flat suburbs southwest of Detroit.
KDTW.w: Detroit is the Motor City: cars driving through snowy winters.

t: Three runways: a long northeast–southwest one and two parallel east–west ones.
The Franklin Mountains rise just to the west, with desert and the border city of Ciudad Juárez across the Rio Grande to the south.
Fort Bliss's Biggs Army Airfield lies on the northeast side of the field.
KELP.w: El Paso is known for its spicy Tex-Mex food and chile peppers.

t: Three runways: two long parallel ones running northeast–southwest and a shorter east–west one that crosses them.
The New Jersey Turnpike runs along the east side, and Port Newark and Elizabeth's stacks of container ships and containers lie just beyond.
The Manhattan skyline is visible about ten miles to the northeast.
KEWR.w: Newark's code EWR doesn't match its name, so this is a pure memory trick: evade the waiting rooms.

t: Two parallel runways running northwest–southeast.
Flat San Joaquin Valley farmland, with fields and orchards in a patchwork all around.
On the northeast side of Fresno, near the suburb of Clovis, with the Sierra Nevada far in the distance.
KFAT.w: Fresno is California farm country, famous for almonds and raisins.

t: Two parallel runways running east–west, with the Atlantic Ocean only a couple of miles to the east.
Port Everglades, with its cruise ships and cranes, sits right next to the airport's southeast side.
A tightly packed urban grid of Dania Beach, Hollywood and Fort Lauderdale surrounds the field.
KFLL.w: Fort Lauderdale is a beach city, so lazy floating fits.

t: Two runways cross: a long northeast–southwest runway and a shorter east–west one.
Sits on a flat, forested plateau west of Spokane, with pine trees all around the airport.
Fairchild Air Force Base, with its long runway and refueling tankers, is a few miles to the west.
KGEG.w: Spokane's odd code GEG comes from the old Geiger Field; eagles gliding just helps the letters stick.

t: Three runways: a long east–west one with a shorter parallel one beside it, and a north–south runway crossing them.
Interstate 96 runs along the airport's north side.
Sits southeast of downtown Grand Rapids, with farmland and wooded suburbs around it.
KGRR.w: Grand Rapids sits on the Grand River.

t: Three runways: two long parallel ones running northeast–southwest and a northwest–southeast runway that crosses them.
FedEx's hub is here, so a big cargo ramp full of FedEx jets sits beside the terminal.
Sits between Greensboro and Winston-Salem in North Carolina's rolling, wooded Piedmont.
KGSO.w: Greensboro has “green” in its name, so growing things fit.

t: Three short runways forming a triangle: one runs northeast–southwest and two parallel ones run northwest–southeast.
A compact airport inside the city of Houston, with Interstate 45 (the Gulf Freeway) passing just west of it.
Surrounded by neighborhoods and industrial blocks, with no large body of water in sight.
KHOU.w: Houston is Space City, home of NASA, so something is always orbiting.

t: Four runways: three long parallel ones running north–south and a diagonal runway.
The main terminal is a long, curved building with a sweeping roof, and midfield concourses are reached by trains.
The Udvar-Hazy air and space museum, with its giant hangar, sits on the airport's southwest side.
KIAD.w: IAD stands for International Airport Dulles.

t: Five runways: three parallel ones running east–west and two parallel ones running northwest–southeast.
The terminals (A, B, C, D, E) are arranged around a central hub and linked by a train.
Far north of downtown Houston, surrounded by thick pine woods and suburbs.
KIAH.w: IAH stands for Intercontinental Airport Houston; astronauts nod to NASA in Houston.

t: Three runways: two long parallel ones running northeast–southwest and a shorter one running northwest–southeast.
FedEx has a major hub here, so a large cargo ramp sits on the field next to the terminal.
Interstate 70 runs along the airport's north side, southwest of downtown Indianapolis.
KIND.w: Indianapolis hosts the Indy 500, so nimble drivers fit.

t: Two runways that do not cross, a long east–west one and a shorter northwest–southeast one.
Far north of downtown Jacksonville, surrounded by dense pine forest and creeks.
Interstate 95 passes close to the airport on its west side.
KJAX.w: “Jax” is Jacksonville's nickname, and Florida has alligators.

t: Four runways in two crossing pairs: two parallel ones running northwest–southeast and two parallel ones running northeast–southwest.
Jamaica Bay's marshes and islands wrap around the north, east and south sides, with the Atlantic beyond.
The terminals form a loop around a big central parking area, with the old swooping TWA Flight Center among them.
KJFK.w: The airport is named for John F. Kennedy.

t: Four runways: two long parallel ones running east–west and two parallel ones running north-northeast to south-southwest.
The Las Vegas Strip, with its towers and the pyramid of the Luxor, runs right along the airport's east end.
Brown desert all around, with mountains in the distance on every side.
KLAS.w: Las Vegas is the gambling capital: luck and spinning slots.

t: Four parallel runways running east–west, in two close pairs with the terminals between them.
The Pacific Ocean is right at the west end, with beaches, dunes and the El Segundo refinery just beyond.
The terminals form a U-shaped loop around a central road, with the flying-saucer shaped Theme Building in the middle.
KLAX.w: Avocados are a California staple; the xylophones just give you the X.

t: Two short runways cross in an X, both about 7,000 ft.
Water on several sides: Flushing Bay to the east and Bowery Bay to the west and north.
The Grand Central Parkway runs along the south side, and Citi Field and the Unisphere in Flushing Meadows are just southeast.
KLGA.w: LaGuardia's runways end at the water, so landings need to be graceful.

t: Three runways: a long northwest–southeast runway crossed by two shorter parallel east–west runways.
A low-slung airport in the middle of Long Beach, with Signal Hill, a hill dotted with oil wells, just to the southwest.
Dense suburbs all around, with the Port of Long Beach cranes a few miles to the south.
Three runways: two parallel ones running almost north–south, and a shorter east–west runway that crosses the western one.
Far north of downtown Kansas City on flat farmland near the Missouri River.
Older imagery shows three half-circle terminals in a row; the new single terminal opened in 2023.
KMCI.w: MCI stands for Mid-Continent International; the cheeseburgers are just a memory hook.

t: Four parallel runways running north–south, two on each side of the terminal complex.
The main terminal is surrounded by four separate gate buildings (airsides), and a newer terminal sits to the south.
Flat Florida scrub and many small lakes all around, southeast of downtown Orlando.
KMCO.w: MCO comes from the old McCoy Air Force Base; Orlando means Disney cartoons and SeaWorld orcas.

t: A compact airport in a tight city grid, covering about one square mile, with four short runways crossing each other in a tangle.
Houses and streets press right up against all four sides of the field, and the Orange Line train ends at its northeast corner.
The longest runway is only about 6,500 ft, which is short for a major airport.
KMDW.w: Midway is a small, compact airport, hence “dinky”.

t: Four runways: three long parallel ones running north–south and a shorter east–west runway.
FedEx's world hub dominates the field: a huge cargo ramp lined with FedEx jets and sorting buildings, far larger than the passenger terminal.
The Mississippi River is about ten miles to the west, and the Mississippi state line is a few miles south.
KMEM.w: Memphis is Elvis's hometown and a home of the blues.

t: Four runways: three parallel ones running east–west and a diagonal runway that crosses the longest one.
The terminal is a very long U shape with concourses (D, E, F, G, H, J) stretching along both arms.
A dense city grid surrounds it, with highways on the west side and Biscayne Bay and the downtown skyline about seven miles to the east.
KMIA.w: Miami is known for sun, beaches and nightlife.

t: Five runways laid out in a star: several pairs cross each other at different angles.
Sits south of downtown Milwaukee, with Lake Michigan about five miles to the east.
Flat, built-up suburbs on every side.
KMKE.w: Milwaukee is famous for its beer.

t: Four runways: a long northeast–southwest runway crossed by two parallel northwest–southeast runways, and a short north–south one.
Sits where the Minnesota and Mississippi Rivers meet, with Fort Snelling's wooded bluffs just to the northeast.
Interstate 494 runs along the south side, and the huge Mall of America is just southeast of the field.
Two runways that do not cross, a long one running east-southeast to west-northwest and a shorter north–south one.
Sits in Kenner, west of New Orleans, with Interstate 10 passing just south of the field.
Lake Pontchartrain is a few miles to the north, and the Mississippi River curves a few miles to the south.
KMSY.w: New Orleans is Mardi Gras country; MSY comes from the old Moisant Stock Yards.

t: Just one long runway, running north–south.
Surrounded by golf courses, resorts and shopping strips of the Grand Strand, with the Atlantic beaches about three miles to the east.
Flat, low coastal land with a sprinkling of ponds and woods.
KMYR.w: Myrtle Beach is a beach town, so sunscreen is the hook.

t: Sits right on San Francisco Bay, with water on the south and west sides and the main runway pointing out toward the bay.
Two groups of runways: one long main runway along the bay and a cluster of shorter ones to the north.
The Oakland Coliseum and arena sit just east of the field, and the cranes of the Port of Oakland are just north.
KOAK.w: Oakland was home to the Athletics baseball team (the A's).

t: Four runways: three long parallel ones running north–south, a diagonal one, and a short extra runway.
The FAA's Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center, a large campus of buildings, sits beside the airport.
Flat red-soil Oklahoma plains southwest of downtown Oklahoma City, with farms and fields around.
Three runways: two parallel ones running northwest–southeast crossed by a north–south runway.
Sits on the Missouri River floodplain, with the river just east of the field and the little oxbow Carter Lake next to its northeast corner.
Downtown Omaha's skyline is about three miles to the southwest.
KOMA.w: Omaha is famous for its steaks.

t: Two parallel runways running east–west.
Hemmed in by huge warehouses and distribution centers on all sides, including UPS's big hub, with the San Gabriel Mountains looming to the north.
Interstate 10 passes north of the airport, in the flat Inland Empire east of Los Angeles.
KONT.w: No local link: ordering nachos tonight just spells O-N-T.

t: Eight runways, the most of any US airport: six parallel ones running east–west and two shorter diagonals that cross them.
Interstate 190 runs straight into the middle of the airport from the east, and a tight grid of Chicago suburbs surrounds it.
Terminals 1, 2 and 3 form the central cluster around a big roadway hub.
KORD.w: Chicago is famous for deep-dish pizza, and ORD comes from the old Orchard Field.

t: Two runways cross in an X, a long northeast–southwest one and a short northwest–southeast one.
Tidal creeks, inlets and the Elizabeth and Lafayette Rivers wind through the surrounding Hampton Roads neighborhoods.
The big Norfolk Naval Station piers, with gray warships, lie a few miles to the northwest.
KORF.w: Norfolk is home to the world's largest naval base, with lots of Navy ships.

t: Three runways: a long east–west one with a short parallel one, and a northwest–southeast runway that crosses the long one.
Interstate 95 runs just west of the airport, and the Palm Beach island beaches and Lake Worth lagoon are a few miles to the east.
Flat, green Florida suburbs with golf courses all around.
KPBI.w: Palm Beach is known for its palm-lined beaches.

t: Three runways: two long parallel ones running east–west right along the river, and a shorter northeast–southwest runway that crosses them.
Sits on the south bank of the Columbia River, with Washington State on the far bank and Mount Hood visible to the east.
An Air National Guard fighter base with hangars sits on the east side of the field.
KPDX.w: “Keep Portland Weird” is the city's slogan, and PDX is its nickname.

t: Four runways: three roughly parallel ones running east–west (one of them shorter) and one running north-northwest to south-southeast that crosses them.
Sits on the Delaware River, with the river along the airport's southeast side and the Schuylkill River meeting it nearby.
Interstate 95 runs along the north and east sides, and the sports stadiums are about four miles to the northeast.
KPHL.w: Philadelphia is a hoagie and cheesesteak town.

t: Three parallel runways running east–west.
Sits just east of downtown Phoenix, with the high-rises of downtown to the west and Camelback Mountain visible to the north.
The dry Salt River bed and Tempe Town Lake are just south and southeast of the field.
Two runways: a long north–south one and a shorter northeast–southwest one.
Sits on the shore of Old Tampa Bay on the Pinellas peninsula, with water along its east edge.
Dense suburbs and strip malls surround the field on the west.
KPIE.w: The code PIE spells a dessert; iced espresso carries on the food theme.

t: Four runways: three long parallel ones running east–west and a diagonal one running northwest–southeast.
Far west of downtown Pittsburgh in hilly, wooded country, with a huge flat site cut out of the hills.
The older terminal's gate buildings radiate out in an X shape.
Two runways cross in an X, a north–south one and an east–west one, each about 7,000 ft.
Pensacola Bay is a few miles to the south, with Naval Air Station Pensacola, the Blue Angels' home, on its southern shore.
Flat, sandy Florida panhandle land with pine woods.
KPNS.w: Pensacola has white-sand beaches, so a picnic near the sand fits.

t: Two parallel runways running northwest–southeast, a long one and a short one.
The San Jacinto Mountains rise steeply right behind the airport to the west.
A desert valley with rows of wind turbines in the pass to the northwest.
KPSP.w: Palm Springs is a calm, peaceful desert resort town.

t: Two runways cross in an X, a long northeast–southwest one and a shorter northwest–southeast one.
Interstate 95 skirts the west side of the field, and Greenwich Bay, an arm of Narragansett Bay, lies to the east.
Dense New England suburbs of Warwick, with small lakes and woods all around.
KPVD.w: Providence is known for WaterFire on its downtown rivers, so think paddling.

t: Two runways cross in an X, a long east–west one and a shorter north–south one.
The Maine Turnpike runs along the airport's west side, and Casco Bay with its many islands is a few miles east.
Wooded, low rolling land at the edge of the city of Portland.
KPWM.w: Portland, Maine is famous for its lobster.

t: Three runways: two parallel ones running northeast–southwest and a short one running northwest–southeast.
Umstead State Park, a big green forest, sits right next to the airport on its north side.
Interstate 40 runs along the south side, between the cities of Raleigh and Durham.
KRDU.w: Raleigh–Durham is the Research Triangle, full of researchers and universities.

t: Two runways that do not cross, a long one running north-northwest to south-southeast and a shorter one running nearly north–south.
Sits east of Richmond near Sandston, with Interstate 64 passing just north of the field.
Flat, wooded Virginia land with the James River winding well to the southwest.
KRIC.w: No local link: kings riding in carriages is easy to picture. Richmond also sounds like a royal name.

t: Three runways: two long parallel ones running north–south crossed by a shorter east–west one.
The Sierra Nevada rises just to the west, and brown desert hills lie to the east.
Sits southeast of the casinos of downtown Reno, close to the city center.
KRNO.w: Reno is the “Biggest Little City” of casinos, so Nevada odds fit.

t: Three runways: a long northeast–southwest runway, an east–west runway and a short one between them.
Sits west of downtown Rochester in flat, suburban land, with Lake Ontario about ten miles to the north.
KROC.w: Rochester is the home of Kodak cameras.

t: Just one long runway running northeast–southwest.
Sits inland east of Fort Myers, with Interstate 75 passing just east of the field and swampy preserves and ponds around it.
The Gulf of Mexico is about a dozen miles to the west.
KRSW.w: The airport serves Southwest Florida, where the beaches are made for sunbathing.

t: Just one runway, running east–west, wedged between downtown San Diego and San Diego Bay.
Skyscrapers sit right next to the approach path, and the Marine Corps Recruit Depot borders the northwest side of the field.
Interstate 5 runs along the north side, and the hills of Point Loma are just to the west.
KSAN.w: San Diego is a surfing city.

t: Three runways: a long northeast–southwest runway crossing two parallel ones running northwest–southeast.
Sits north of downtown San Antonio in dense suburbs, with U.S. Highway 281 running along its east side.
Flat Texas Hill Country foothills with a patchwork of neighborhoods and shopping centers all around.
KSAT.w: San Antonio is home to the Alamo.

t: Two runways cross in an X, an east–west one and a north–south one.
Interstate 95 passes just west of the airport.
Surrounded by pine forest and marshy creeks, northwest of downtown Savannah.
KSAV.w: Savannah is known for its antique-filled historic squares and verandas.

t: Just one long runway, running northeast–southwest.
Surrounded by huge warehouses and a big cargo ramp, on the old Norton Air Force Base.
The San Bernardino Mountains rise to the north.
KSBD.w: McDonald's started in San Bernardino, so food is the hook.

t: Three runways: two long parallel ones running almost north–south and a diagonal that crosses them.
UPS's Worldport hub dominates the field, with a huge ramp full of brown-tailed cargo planes bigger than the passenger terminal.
Churchill Downs racetrack sits just north of the airport, south of downtown Louisville.
KSDF.w: Louisville is Kentucky Derby country; SDF comes from the old Standiford Field.

t: Three parallel runways running north–south, with the westernmost one built up on a raised fill embankment.
Sits on a ridge between Puget Sound to the west and Lake Washington to the east, with Interstate 5 along the east side.
Mount Rainier looms to the southeast on a clear day.
Four runways: three parallel ones running east–west and a north–south one that crosses them.
The St. Johns River and Lake Monroe lie a few miles to the northwest.
Surrounded by Sanford's flat, green suburbs and wooded land, northeast of Orlando.
KSFB.w: Sanford is a Florida lakeside town, so sailing is the hook.

t: Four runways in two crossing pairs that form a hash-mark pattern: two parallel ones running east-southeast to west-northwest and two parallel ones running north-northeast to south-southwest.
Sits right on the western shore of San Francisco Bay, with runways pointing out into the water and U.S. Highway 101 along the west side.
The terminals form a horseshoe around a central garage, with the international terminal's big sweeping roof.
KSFO.w: San Francisco is famous for sourdough bread.

t: Two long parallel runways running northwest–southeast, both about 11,000 ft.
Right in the middle of Silicon Valley, ringed by office parks and highways, with Interstate 880 on the east side.
The colorful salt evaporation ponds of the southern bay are visible a few miles to the north.
KSJC.w: San Jose is the heart of Silicon Valley.

t: Three parallel runways running north–south.
The Great Salt Lake and its flat salt marshes lie to the northwest, and the Wasatch Mountains rise just east of the valley.
Interstate 80 runs along the south side, with downtown Salt Lake City about four miles east.
KSLC.w: Salt Lake City has great skiing, so hot cocoa fits.

t: Two parallel runways running north–south, each about 8,600 ft.
Sits in the flat Sacramento Valley, a patchwork of rice fields and farmland, with Interstate 5 along the east side.
About ten miles northwest of downtown Sacramento.
KSMF.w: Sacramento calls itself America's Farm-to-Fork capital.

t: One main runway, running northeast–southwest, only about 5,700 ft, short for a jet airport, with a tiny second runway beside it.
Hemmed in by freeways: Interstate 405 along its northeast side and Highway 55 to the west.
Surrounded by Irvine's office towers and Orange County suburbs.
KSNA.w: Santa Ana is in Orange County, citrus country, so fruit is the hook.

t: Two runways cross in an X, a long northwest–southeast one and a shorter northeast–southwest one.
The grounds of the Ringling Museum and Sarasota Bay lie just southwest of the field, with barrier islands like Longboat Key beyond.
A flat grid of Florida neighborhoods and U.S. 41 runs along the west side.
KSRQ.w: Sarasota is a relaxed beach and arts town.

t: Four runways: three parallel ones running northwest–southeast and a northeast–southwest one that crosses them.
The main terminal has a row of thin concrete vaults, a 1950s design by Minoru Yamasaki.
Interstate 70 runs past the northeast side, and the Missouri River is a few miles north.
KSTL.w: St. Louis is known for the Gateway Arch landmark.

t: Two runways cross in an X, a long east–west one and a shorter northwest–southeast one.
Sits northeast of downtown Syracuse, with Interstate 81 along its west side.
Onondaga Lake lies about four miles to the west.
KSYR.w: Syracuse gets huge snowfall every winter.

t: Three runways: two parallel ones running north–south and a shorter east–west one that crosses the shorter of them.
Sits on the northeastern shore of Tampa Bay, with water along its west side and Interstate 275 along its east side.
A central main terminal is surrounded by separate gate buildings (airsides) reached by shuttle.
KTPA.w: Tampa's Gasparilla festival is a pirate invasion.

t: Three runways: two parallel ones running north–south crossed by a shorter east–west one.
American Airlines' big maintenance base, with a large hangar complex full of silver jets, sits on the field.
The Arkansas River winds west of the airport, and Interstate 244 passes just south.
Two runways that do not cross, a long one running northwest–southeast and a shorter one running northeast–southwest.
A desert basin ringed by mountains: the Santa Rita Mountains to the southeast, the Santa Catalinas to the northeast and the Tucson Mountains to the northwest.
The Raytheon missile plant, with its big buildings, is right next to the airport.
